L26@P0: TREATMENT:
L27@P0: The starting dose of the drugs detailed below may be adjusted downward by the prescribing clinician, using their
L28@P0: independent medical judgement, to consider each patient’s individual clinical circumstances.
L29@P0: DOXOrubicin is administered on days 1-3 and CISplatin on Day 1 of a 21 day cycle for six cycles (THREE cycles
L30@P0: usually given pre-operatively and THREE cycles given post-operatively following review of pathology).
L31@P0: Facilities to treat anaphylaxis MUST be present when systemic anticancer therapy (SACT) is administered.
L32@P0: Note: Administration volumes and fluids have been standardised to facilitate electronic prescribing system builds.
L33@P0: ELIGIBILITY:
L34@P0:  Indications as above
L35@P0:  ECOG status 0-2
L36@P0:  Adequate organ function

L40@P0: 2 1
L41@P0: bCISplatin 100mg/m2
L42@P0: IV infusion 1000mL NaCl 0.9% over 2 hours
L43@P0: aLifetime cumulative dose of doxorubicin is 450mg/m2
L44@P0: In establishing the maximal cumulative dose of an anthracycline, consideration should be given to the risk factors outlined belowi and to the age
L45@P0: of the patient.
L46@P0: b Pre and post hydration therapy required for CISplatin
L47@P0: See local hospital policy recommendations.
L48@P0: Suggested prehydration for CISplatin therapy:
L49@P0: Administer 10mmol magnesium sulphate (MgSO4) ((+/-KCl 20mmol/L if indicated) in 1000 mL NaCl 0.9% over 60-120 minutes. (Refer to relevant local
L50@P0: hospital policy for advice on administration of electrolyte infusions).
L51@P0: Administer CISplatin as described above
L52@P0: Post hydration: Administer 1000 mL NaCl 0.9% over 60 minutes
L53@P0: Mannitol 10% may be used as per local policy to induce diuresis, although there is no conclusive evidence that this is required. The routine use of
L54@P0-1: furosemide to increase urine flow is not recommended unless there is evidence of fluid overload.NCCP SACT Regimen

L6@P0-1:  Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0
L7@P1: Publish Date: November 27, 2017
L8@P1: Introduction
L9@P1: The NCI Common Terminology Criteria for
L10@P1: Adverse Events is a descriptive terminology which
L11@P1: can be utilized for Adverse Event (AE) reporting. A
L12@P1: grading (severity) scale is provided for each AE
L13@P1: term.
L14@P1: SOC
L15@P1: System Organ Class (SOC), the highest level of the
L16@P1: MedDRA1 hierarchy, is identified by anatomical or
L17@P1: physiological system, etiology, or purpose (e.g.,
L18@P1: SOC Investigations for laboratory test results).
L19@P1: CTCAE terms are grouped by MedDRA Primary
L20@P1: SOCs. Within each SOC, AEs are listed and
L21@P1: accompanied by descriptions of severity (Grade).
L22@P1: CTCAE Terms
L23@P1: An Adverse Event (AE) is any unfavorable and
L24@P1: unintended sign (including an abnormal
L25@P1: laboratory finding), symptom, or disease
L26@P1: temporally associated with the use of a medical
L27@P1: treatment or procedure that may or may not be
L28@P1: considered related to the medical treatment or
L29@P1: procedure. An AE is a term that is a unique
L30@P1: representation of a specific event used for
L31@P1: medical documentation and scientific analyses.
L32@P1: Each CTCAE v4.0 term is a MedDRA LLT (Lowest
L33@P1: Level Term).
L34@P1:  1 CTCAE v5.0 incorporates certain elements of the MedDRA terminology. For further details on MedDRA refer to the MedDRA MSSO Web site (https://www.meddra.org/).
L35@P1: Grades
L36@P1: Grade refers to the severity of the AE. The CTCAE
L37@P1: displays Grades 1 through 5 with unique clinical
L38@P1: descriptions of severity for each AE based on this
L39@P1: general guideline:
L40@P1: Grade 1 Mild; asymptomatic or mild
L41@P1: symptoms; clinical or diagnostic
L42@P1: observations only; intervention
L43@P1: not indicated.
L44@P1: Grade 2 Moderate; minimal, local or
L45@P1: noninvasive intervention
L46@P1: indicated; limiting ageappropriate instrumental ADL*.
L47@P1: Grade 3 Severe or medically significant but not
L48@P1: immediately life-threatening;
L49@P1: hospitalization or prolongation
L50@P1: of hospitalization indicated;
L51@P1: disabling; limiting self care
L52@P1: ADL**.
L53@P1: Grade 4 Life-threatening consequences; urgent
L54@P1: intervention indicated.
L55@P1: Grade 5 Death related to AE.
L56@P1: A Semi-colon indicates ‘or’ within the description
L57@P1: of the grade.
L58@P1: A single dash (-) indicates a Grade is not available.
L59@P1: Not all Grades are appropriate for all AEs.
L60@P1: Therefore, some AEs are listed with fewer than
L61@P1: five options for Grade selection.
L62@P1: Grade 5
L63@P1: Grade 5 (Death) is not appropriate for some AEs
L64@P1: and therefore is not an option.
L65@P1: Definitions
L66@P1: A brief Definition is provided to clarify the
L67@P1: meaning of each AE term. A single dash (-)
L68@P1: indicates a Definition is not available.
L69@P1: Navigational Notes
L70@P1: A Navigational Note is used to assist the reporter
L71@P1: in choosing a correct AE. It may list other AEs that
L72@P1: should be considered in addition to or in place of
L73@P1: the AE in question. A single dash (-) indicates a
L74@P1: Navigational Note has not been defined for the AE
L75@P1: term.
L76@P1: Activities of Daily Living (ADL)
L77@P1: *Instrumental ADL refer to preparing meals,
L78@P1: shopping for groceries or clothes, using the
L79@P1: telephone, managing money, etc.
L80@P1: **Self care ADL refer to bathing, dressing and
L81@P1: undressing, feeding self, using the toilet, taking
L82@P1-2: medications, and not bedridden.Table of Contents
